passage.quote:
When semantic review is delegated to an inexpensive model, it is a separate
review task from generation.

summary: Review fixed candidates against pinned PTX passages in a separate model invocation, keeping proof checking and coordinator acceptance independent.
Record exact request and response identities, failures, usage and unknown costs without silent retries or model substitution.
Evaluate concrete fault detection and false alarms on blinded cases; retain vendor-bearing requests and responses locally.
Freeze fresh evaluation cases before requests and keep fixture evidence distinct from actual worker-candidate reviews.
remaining: Recorded fixed-context OpenRouter review, adjudicated development trials, and an adjudicated frozen six-case fixture suite are implemented. A runner-enforced total wall-time deadline, general reviewer-quality evidence, tool-using repository review and automatic integration remain outside the implemented route.

from.quote:
A review packet fixes a repository commit, candidate file hashes, supporting
interfaces, source section hashes, and project-authored obligations. The vendor
source is read only from the verified local manual. The same packet can be sent
to different reviewers. Evaluation labels, mutation descriptions, original
acceptance verdicts and generating-model conversations are excluded from the
request. Candidate text is review material, not instructions to the reviewer.
The first implementation reviews a supplied context without tools; it records
this limitation instead of claiming the reviewer inspected the whole repository.

from.quote:
Reports identify the obligations considered, findings tied to candidate locations
and source anchors, and remaining uncertainty. References and report structure
are checked mechanically. Such validation does not establish that a finding is
true. The coordinator adjudicates findings before using them for acceptance.

Small adaptive trials describe those cases, not a general accuracy
estimate or justification for automatic integration.
